facts.subject: language
facts.text: The word 'pyjamas' comes from words in Hindi and Urdu.

facts.subject: language
facts.text: The word 'emoji' comes from Japanese.

facts.subject: language
facts.text: Sign languages are real languages that use hands, faces and bodies instead of sound.

facts.subject: language
facts.text: Thousands of languages are spoken around the world.

facts.subject: math
facts.text: A googol is the number 1 followed by 100 zeros.

facts.subject: math
facts.text: The equals sign (=) was first used in 1557 by a Welsh mathematician called Robert Recorde.

facts.subject: math
facts.text: Going around a circle is a bit more than 3 times as far as going across it. This number is called pi.

facts.subject: math
facts.text: A prime number can only be divided exactly by 1 and by itself. 7 is a prime number.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: Spiders are not insects. A spider has eight legs.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: Sharks have skeletons made of cartilage, not bone.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: Mars looks red because of iron oxide, a kind of rust, in its dust.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: A bolt of lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.

facts.subject: world
facts.text: Mount Everest is the highest mountain above sea level.

facts.subject: world
facts.text: Antarctica is the coldest continent.

facts.subject: world
facts.text: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world.

facts.subject: world
facts.text: Russia is the biggest country in the world by area.

facts.subject: health
facts.text: About 60 percent of the human body is water.

facts.subject: health
facts.text: Every person has different fingerprints, even twins.

facts.subject: health
facts.text: At rest, a grown-up's heart beats about 72 times a minute.

facts.subject: health
facts.text: Brushing your teeth helps remove plaque, which can cause tooth decay.

facts.subject: digital
facts.text: Douglas Engelbart gave the first public demonstration of a computer mouse in 1968.

facts.subject: digital
facts.text: A byte is made of 8 bits.

facts.subject: digital
facts.text: The first text message was sent in 1992 and said 'Merry Christmas'.

facts.subject: digital
facts.text: The name Google comes from the word googol, a very large number.

facts.subject: money
facts.text: In parts of Africa and Asia, cowrie shells were once used as money.

facts.subject: money
facts.text: A mint is a place where coins are made.

facts.subject: money
facts.text: When you save money in a bank, the bank may pay you a little extra called interest.

facts.subject: money
facts.text: The first paper money was used in China many hundreds of years ago.

facts.subject: thinking
facts.text: Chess comes from an Indian game called chaturanga, played about 1,400 years ago.

facts.subject: thinking
facts.text: In noughts and crosses (tic-tac-toe), if both players play perfectly, the game is a draw.

facts.subject: thinking
facts.text: A Sudoku puzzle uses the numbers 1 to 9.

facts.subject: thinking
facts.text: An optical illusion is a picture that tricks your brain into seeing something that is not really there.

facts.subject: arts
facts.text: The Mona Lisa is a painting that hangs in a museum in Paris called the Louvre.

facts.subject: arts
facts.text: Vincent van Gogh painted The Starry Night in 1889.

facts.subject: arts
facts.text: A cartoon is made of many drawings shown one after another very fast.

facts.subject: arts
facts.text: A big orchestra can have more than 100 players.

facts.subject: computing
facts.text: Ada Lovelace is often called the first computer programmer.

facts.subject: computing
facts.text: Long ago, the word 'computer' meant a person who did sums for a job.

facts.subject: computing
facts.text: Scratch, a free way to learn coding with colourful blocks, was made at a university called MIT.

facts.subject: computing
facts.text: The brain of a computer is a chip called the CPU.
